title: Config Editor: Adaptive Caching & Batching UI (prototype + review)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Design an in-console configuration editor that helps engineers and SREs choose caching and batching settings that balance latency SLOs and per-token cost. The UI should surface Redwood Optimize recommendations, show an impact preview (latency vs cost), provide safe guardrails (recommended presets and hard limits for guests/teams), and make it easy to test with a simulated workload preview. Background: Customers frequently ask how to tune batching and prefix/KV cache settings. Engineering teams (serving-runtime and Optimize) will expose APIs for 'suggested profiles' and a simulation endpoint. This ticket covers the interactive editor flows, on-screen explainers, presets, access controls, and the prototype for stakeholder review. Out of scope: backend API implementation, actual rollout automation (will be a follow-up ENG ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Clickable prototype demonstrating these flows: select model variant -> view recommended profile -> adjust batch size and cache TTL -> preview estimated cost and p50/p95 latency impact
Contextual explainers for each parameter (why it matters, when to increase/decrease) available as hover tooltips and a side 'Why this matters' panel
Presets: 'Low latency', 'Balanced', 'Low cost' with descriptions and one-click apply
Guardrails UI: ability to set org-level max batch/ttl and team-level editable presets with warnings when changes affect SLOs
Accessibility: keyboard nav, screen reader labels, and color contrast meet WCAG AA
Design handoff assets (Figma frames + tokens) and a clear engineering spec linking to ENG-2176 for API integration
tasks: Design: produce 3 high-fidelity candidate flows (compact inline editor, side-panel advanced editor, full-screen simulation playground)
PM: validate wording for 'cost estimate' and 'latency estimate' to avoid SLA promises
Eng: confirm simulation API contract and fields with ENG-2176
Create copy variants for tooltips and guardrail warnings and run microcopy review
comments: 2026-02-20 - Asha Patel: Kickoff note. Met with PM (Ravi Kumar) and ENG (Sofia Morales). Confirmed the need for presets + simulation preview. Agreed to prototype three candidate layouts.

2026-02-26 - Asha Patel: Explorations complete. Uploaded three concepts to Figma and flagged frames for stakeholder review. Key trade-offs: inline editor keeps context but hides simulation; full-screen shows rich simulation but interrupts workflow.

2026-03-02 - Ravi Kumar (PM): Prefer side-panel advanced editor as default; it provides quick access and keeps the route context. PM asks that cost delta be shown relative to baseline profile and not absolute dollars for legal simplicity.

2026-03-04 - Sofia Morales (ENG): Confirmed simulation endpoint can return estimated p50/p95 latency and cost-per-1000-tokens under current cluster load model. Provided API stub in ENG-2176. Noted the need for debounce on inputs to avoid simulation spam.
2026-03-06 - Asha: Incorporated engineer notes. Added input debounce UX and optimistic local preview before simulation returns. Created accessibility checklist for keyboard interactions.

2026-03-08 - Design review: Internal feedback from Growth and Support. Support asked for a 'Why this change will affect my bill' short explainer panel. Growth suggested showing 'trimming suggestions' for extreme low-cost presets.

2026-03-10 - Liam Chen (assignee): Submitted prototype link and design spec to ENG-PR for review. Requested API clarification on relation between cache TTL and KV cache size. Next: sync with infra on rollout guardrail enforcement points.
